# P05 history attribution across two releases

Secondary analysis of published local forecast ledgers. The parent aggregate results were already public and known before this protocol. Freeze this specification before scoring new history strata. The local hash provides integrity and the sequence of analysis, with no independent timestamp or untouched confirmation.

## Eligibility and shared endpoint

Use the pinned pyKT ASSIST2015 official test learners and the pinned EdNet KT1 development screen (SHA-256 learner buckets 70–79), retaining all forecasted responses. EdNet training and tuning learners are available for provenance checks. Reserved buckets 80–99 stay compressed. Both endpoints are binary current-response correctness conditional on an available current opportunity and at least one eligible prior response. Compute event-weighted natural-log loss, with probabilities clipped to [1e-7, 1−1e-7]. ASSIST uses the released single-concept ordered learner prefixes, where prediction begins at zero-based step 1. EdNet uses strictly completed earlier solving bundles at the current bundle’s first presentation, with the published first tag and 160-row horizon. Align records within each release by the original event key, verifying correctness and exact coverage against the releases. Learners and event keys have source-local identities.

Count eligible prior responses on each event, using the ASSIST prefix length or the reconstructed EdNet completed-bundle history length, before any model-specific window cap. Report all events and disjoint depth bins of 1–16, 17–31 and 32 or more. The 16 boundary corresponds to the EdNet attention window and 32+ is the primary long-history stratum. The depth bins measure observed platform history under each release’s sampling and availability policy. They do not align elapsed time, knowledge concepts, or item difficulty. Retain every eligible forecast and every signed loss contrast. Bin composition and repeated skill support will be reported to explain interpretation.

## Fixed contrasts

Positive gain is control minus candidate loss on exactly the same events. On ASSIST, use full_blend against skill_mean, logistic, dkt, full, short and short_blend. The closest feature contrast is short_blend. Also compare the matched trees (short minus full) to isolate the history feature comparison from blend weight changes. Both ASSIST trees already have pooled full-prefix histories. The increment is same-skill run length and current within-run success/failure streaks. The word “short” in the ledger refers to the feature list, not a truncated input history.

On EdNet use blend_joint against every other archived model on the same screen in temporal, published_simplekt, item_ability and distractors, including all four tree/attention blends (with the candidate as reference), upstream item-aware and skill-only simpleKT, the four item-ability variants and both option-lag variants. Use blend_clock as the closest feature contrast. Also compare clock minus joint for the matched trees. The EdNet tree increment includes intervening count and outcomes since the previous same primary skill, recent same-part/different-skill statistics and switches. It is a related but different exposure. Clock-only already uses full-prefix counts, elapsed time and recency. Keep coincident model columns in the register. The strongest observed control means lowest control loss on the reporting stratum. It is a descriptive rank. Inference uses the fixed comparisons, not a statistic for a newly selected control.

In each corpus report all fixed contrasts on the four scopes (overall and three bins). Also report the 32+ minus 1–16 gain interaction for each closest feature contrast, with the same learners sampled across both bins. Report event and learner counts, class balance, and repeated-skill support. Use 20,000 paired learner-cluster bootstrap draws per source, sampling source learners with replacement and keeping their complete event contributions, with seeds 731 and 732. Use percentile intervals with a Bonferroni 95% family across all contrasts and scopes and both interactions. Report the .015-nat practical margin and whether each observed gain reaches it with a positive simultaneous lower bound. A small or uncertain gain does not establish equivalence. Report any absence of events or undefined bootstrap denominator rather than changing strata.

## Claim boundary

This is a cross-source comparison of performance patterns after source-local fitting. A sign or depth pattern can recur descriptively for related features. A faithful replication of the exact ASSIST feature claim requires matched same-skill run and streak ablations in both datasets. A causal attribution to longer access needs a matched model with only the history horizon varied. Frozen-model transfer would require predictions from an unchanged source-trained model on the other release under a defined item/skill mapping and common availability policy. Existing ledgers allow neither the exact replication nor frozen transfer. Report missing comparator forecasts from the P05 register and do not substitute performance from another cohort. No fitting or GPU use in this analysis.
